newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - May 16.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN Australia's new national rowing coach, Brian Richardson, said yesterday he believes this year's pairing of Robert Jahrling and Staurt McRae, who will be competing at this year's world championships at France, can emulate the success of their predecessors, Olympic silver medallists David Weightman and Rob Scott. Page 24.

-- In comments which follow the three-day hearing involving Greg Williams, his club Carlton and the Australian Football League, Supreme Court Justice John Hedigan said yesterday he was concerned he might be setting a dangerous precedent if he overturned Willams' nine-match suspension. Page 24.

-- In an indication yesterday Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor may be regaining his form, he drove and cut his way to an unbeaten 25 when opening the batting against the Duke of Norfolk's XI as Australia moved to 0-70 after an hour's play. The match, payed in Arundel, marked the start of Australia's tour of England. Page 24.

THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD Following an accusation from a New Zealand talk-show host that Australia had "cheated" the Kiwis out of a tri-series win when a last-minute try by the New Zealanders was disallowed in Wednesday night's match against New South Wales at Bruce Stadium, SuperLeague executive Ian Frykberg admitted he could sympathise with the Kiwis' frustration, but said the decision cannot be changed. Page 46.

-- A day after top seeds Pete Sampras and Michael Chang made their exits from the Italian Open, Australia's Scott Draper, dubbed the 'bionic man' of tennis for his strength, achieved a major career win yesterday, beating third-seeded Thomas Muster 7-6 (7-4) -7 7-5. Page 45.

-- Returning after a three-match suspension, prop Richard Harry has been named in the New South Wales front row against Auckland in the rugby union Super 12 clash against Auckland tomorrow night, while Andrew Heath's hopes of winning a Test berth were dashedafter selectors found fault with his mobility and his general work. Page 45.

THE AGE The Sydney Swans' hopes of leaving Football Park with a win against Adelaide tomorrow were dealt a blow last night when club legend Tony Lockett was left out of the side after failing to overcome an ongoing thigh complaint, while fellow forward Craig O'Bren was omitted as he nurses a shoulder injury. Page D3.

-- Under the 1997-98 cricket season draw announced yesterday by the Australian Cricket Board, Sydney has regained the traditional New Year Test match, while Adelaide has lost the Australia Day weekend for its Test match, with that weekend being taken up by limited overs fixtures. Page D10.

-- According to Australian cycling coach James Victor, the three new members of the women's eight-strong road cycling team, Juanita Feldhahn and Hayley Huch from Queensland and Kim Palmer of the Australian Capital Territory, may have a shortened European tou, depending on their ability to cope with the women's Tour de France. Page D11.

THE HERALD SUN As part of an investigation into ways for umpires to alert umpires' observers during a game to questionable incidents, the Australian Football League is considering wiring umpires with transmitters. AFL football operations manager Ian Collins said he was also looking into a change of procedure so umpires, checking for reportable incidents, would not have to look at video footage after games. Page 104.

-- Despite losing captain Gary O'Donnell, Che Cockatoo-Collins and David Calthorpe with hamstring injuries, morale at Essendon has been boosted with the news that AFL champion James Hird and mid-fielder Michael Long will be returning to the side for Sunday'sclash against St Kilda. Page 100.

-- Leading Australian jockey Darren Beadman has confirmed he has been spoken to by agents from the Hong Kong Independent Commission Against Corruption, but said they were just going over old ground and he couldn't help them. The ICAC later told AJC chief steard Ray Murrihy it would not be seeking further talks with Beadman. Page 102.

THE DAILY TELEGRAPH South Queensland rugby league players last night reacted angrily to news from club chief executive Eric Laakso that the players' 1997 match payments were being held back. The move comes after the players were told earlier this year they had to win matchesand boost home crowds to receive their payments of A$5000 - the first grade side failed to live up to the ultimatum, winning only one of its ten ARL matches. Page 125.

-- Sydney's rebel marathon organisers suffered a major blow yesterday when the New South Wales Police Service State Operations Planning Unit denied having given the "International Sydney Harbour Marathon" the required police traffic authority approval. Page 21.

-- Rising young stayer Yippyio, the winner of the Queensland Guineas horse race earlier this year, clashes with fellow Melbourne Cup hopeful Marble Halls tomorrow in the Group 2 A$200,000 Grand Prix Stakes at Eagle Farm, in a showdown being billed as the rac of the winter carnival so far. Page 119.
